reviews.comment: I probably learned more in this class than any other class at Tamu. Not sure about her bad reviews from the Fall, I think her practice tests are great and she gives lots of guidance on how to study. I have a 3.1 GPA and got in A in this by going to most classes and moderately studying for exams. Highly recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grades are made up of 5 problem sets that are like homework that she explains well in class before they are due, a midterm, and a final exam. You get a cheat sheet for the midterm & final as well as practice tests. She really sets you up for success, and everyone should take her. Material is hard, but as long as you go to class, you'll be great.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never wrote a rate my professor review so that should show you how bad she is. She is a very intelligent lady with great hair I might add, but she is a terrible teacher. I learned almost nothing from her lectures and tests were 50x more complicated than the practice tests. She curved at the end, bc if she hadn't the avg would have been a 50.

Li is extremely intelligent, almost too intelligent to be teaching an intermediate level course. The class started off very rocky. She did improve and take suggestions to make lectures more manageable. This is an extremely math heavy course. If you do not feel confident in your business calculus and stats ability, I would take another teacher.

Avoid at all costs. She is a GPA killer. The mean of the grade distribution for her class was significantly less than the other prof. The problem sets will have you questioning your degree choice and you'll walk away from this class wishing you were a communications major. Significantly harder than acct 327.

one of the hardest professors i have taken at texas a&m. there was a monumental difference in grading distributions from this professor and the other prof who was teaching this (63 v 90). be prepared to work hard

This was her first semester teachering Finc 351 and the first exam was really rough (told by a friend our sections averaged 25 pts lower than other profs). However, she improved as the course went on and listened to the feedback she recieved. Would try to get a different prof if possible but not the end of the world if she's the only one.

Dr. Li is extremely intelligent and a great professor. The class is very statistics and math heavy but nothing too difficult. If you complete and understand the problem sets, you will be fine on the exams (the tests are practically the same problems). Class is weighted exam heavy so keep that in mind.

The lectures started a little rocky, but she took the feedback that was given to her and improved her lectures tremendously. She also adjusted the test difficulty after seeing the results on the first test, showing that she is a flexible and understanding teacher.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty great professor. She took feedback seriously and adjusted her teaching methods accommodatingly. She gives plenty of time for problem sets and is open to answering questions and providing clarification. The material is difficult, but she explains it well and checks to see if everyone understands. Don't slack off and expect to do well.

Fulin Li is the worst professor I have had at TAMU. Problem sets take a long time, tests are wild, and she really doesn't give partial credit. Nobody knew what was going on in that class because her lectures were all over the place and super fast paced. Please take anyone but her. If you think FINC 341/361 or ACCT 327 are bad, do not take her.
